messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — PAGER: runtime-gateway increased 5xx rate > 8% in us-east-1. Pager: eng-oncall. Incident: INC-2026-451. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-451
Alex Chen: I’m primary until 12:30pt, currently on my way in. Anyone able to take initial triage? I can look at tracing after quick handoff.
Maria Gomez: I’ll take primary for the next 30m. Sam, you’re secondary? @Samir Patel
Samir Patel: on it — taking secondary. Quick note: is this routing to runtime or infra? I’m seeing RTG hosts throwing OOMs in k8s events.
Jin Park: runtime team — we pushed a small model-kernel change 1hr ago. I’m standing by to check model variants + kernel selection logs. @Alex Chen send the deployment id pls.
Alex Chen: deployment id: deploy-rtg-2026-09-03-1423. Also, load looks fine on infra boxes but some pods restart loops.
Maria Gomez: ok, plan: Sam do quick k8s pod checks (OOMs, restarts), Jin validate whether the kernel change could affect KV cache eviction. Lia, flag support for customer-impact blips.
Samir Patel: kubectl output pasted:
```
NAME                                       READY  STATUS             RESTARTS
runtime-gateway-7f9b8f6c4-ptk2q           1/1    Running            3
runtime-gateway-7f9b8f6c4-x9j3l           0/1    CrashLoopBackOff    12
```
OOMKilled on container `rtg-exec`. Memory limits unchanged. Logs show `alloc failed` before crash.
Lia (oncall-support): support here — customer-facing latency spikes reported for 3 customers (account ids masked) since ~14:05 UTC. Not wide, but definitely visible on consoles. I'll add to incident doc.
Jin Park: I'm pulling kernel + allocator logs now. If allocator has regressed, we may need to rollback to model-kernel v3.2.4. Can infra hold scaling while we decide?
ops-bot: Auto-scale policy triggered 3x in us-east-1 for runtime-pool-3. Current capacity: 45/120 pods.
Maria Gomez: Security-oncall — is there any chance this is an exploit or bad input leading to memory exhaustion? @security-oncall
security-oncall: unlikely based on current logs — patterns look consistent with allocation growth, not unusual request shapes. We’ll keep monitoring. No ADT alarms raised.
Samir Patel: I’m attaching snippet showing repeated large tensor allocations in traces: https://logs.redwood/tx/abc123 (shortlink)
Alex Chen: Given OOMs + allocator suspicion, propose: 1) scale down model-kernel rollout (rollback) -> Jin can run a canary rollback to v3.2.4, 2) temporarily increase memory limit for CrashLoop pod to avoid customer impact, 3) notify support with mitigation note.
Jin Park: I can rollback canary now. Will patch the Deployment to image:v3.2.4 for a 5% canary and watch for 3 minutes. If green, promote.
Maria Gomez: Sam, please patch pod memory limit to +25% on the failing node group, lock autoscaler so it doesn't evict during this window.
Samir Patel: done — patched `runtime-gateway` mem limit from 6Gi->7.5Gi in us-east-1 nodepool-rtg. Autoscaler suspended for 15m. 
ops-bot: Autoscaler: policy suspended by samir (15m) — note: manual resume required or will auto-resume at end.
Jin Park: canary rollback started: deploy-rtg-2026-09-03-1423 -> image:v3.2.4 on 3 pods. Monitoring traces.
Maria Gomez: Lia, please add a short customer message: “We’re aware of increased errors for a subset of requests in us-east-1. We’re rolling back a recent runtime change and expect improvement within 10–15 minutes.”
Lia (oncall-support): drafted and queued to OMS for affected customers. CCed account owners.
security-oncall: observing no suspicious IPs; keeping watch on request sizes.
Alex Chen: handoff: Maria will remain primary until 12:30pt as agreed; Jin will be runtime lead, Sam infra lead, Lia will handle customer comms, security-oncall keeps monitoring. We have a 15m check-in — set a calendar reminder.
Maria Gomez: Confirmed. Gaps: nights this week we only have single secondary for runtime (no second infra). Sam can you find a buddy for next night? @Samir Patel
Samir Patel: putting a ping in eng-infra channel to recruit backup. If no response, I’ll extend pager rotation for Thu night.
Jin Park: Canary looks good: no OOMs on the 3 canary pods for 6 min. Promoting to full rollout.
ops-bot: Deployment promoted: runtime-gateway image v3.2.4 -> 42 pods. Rolling update initiated.
Samir Patel: after rollout, I've seen crashloop count drop to 0. Memory pressure reduced in nodepool.
Lia (oncall-support): support notified customers and marked incident as 'investigating -> mitigating' in doc.
Alex Chen: great work team. After we stabilize, please add detailed postmortem notes to INC-2026-451: root cause hypothesis (allocator regression in v3.2.5), timeline, who paged, and clear who did handoff. Also add runbook pointer: https://runbooks.redwood/oncall/runtime-oom.
Maria Gomez: agreed. I’ll own postmortem and ensure next steps for on-call shifts: we need a dedicated secondary for runtime overnight this week. 
security-oncall: one quick follow-up — can we add a guard in runtime that rejects requests whose allocation footprint > X? I'll open a GH PR for an emergency limiter.
Alex Chen: +1. If urgent, mark PR with `security/urgent` label and ping runtime. 
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status: mitigating. Pagers silenced at 14:18 UTC. Next update in 15m or on call change.
Alex Chen: thanks everyone. Staying on until metrics return to baseline, but handing primary to Maria as planned. :thumbsup:
